description: In a heartfelt announcement, Harmanpreet Kaur has declared her resignation as captain of the Indian women's cricket team. Under her guidance, India achieved remarkable feats, including winning a World Cup and securing an Asian Games gold medal. Tributes from stars like Yuvraj Singh, Shafali Verma, and Shikhar Dhawan celebrate her impactful leadership. Despite stepping down, Kaur will continue to represent India, fueled by her enduring passion for cricket.

Trivedi accused the Congress’s first family of running the country like a monarchy. He urged the public and the nation to closely scrutinize the statements of Rahul Gandhi and his party leaders.

title: Missouri couple restored 300 acres into refuge for thriving deer herd
description: Mike and Dana Blevins turned their 300-acre property in Missouri into a thriving habitat for white-tailed deer. After purchasing the land, they implemented habitat management practices supported by the Missouri Department of Conservation. Their efforts contributed to the significant recovery of deer populations in the region, which faced near extinction in the past. As chronic wasting disease poses new challenges, they took part in management efforts to control infections.

title: Wisconsin shopper paid $29 for painting; it later sold for $882,500
description: In a remarkable turn of events, a man from Wisconsin stumbled upon a magnolia painting for just $29 at a rummage sale in the 1990s. A decade later, the artwork was authenticated as the work of esteemed American artist Martin Johnson Heade. Auctioned at Christie’s, it fetched an astonishing $882,500, shattering initial estimates of $300,000 to $500,000.

title: ‘I'm not a cheater’: Coco Gauff hits back at racist abuse after China Open row
description: Coco Gauff faced a wave of racist backlash on social media after her match against Sun Xinran, prompting discussions about sportsmanship and fairness. The match's tension escalated when Gauff paused play over flickering advertising boards, leading to a controversial replay. Despite the negative comments, she highlighted the protocol for video reviews.

George Lucas turned California ranchland into nearly 5,000-acre Skywalker Ranch
description: Nestled in Marin County, Skywalker Ranch is a vast 4,700-acre creative sanctuary brought to life by filmmaker George Lucas. This enchanting retreat features a Victorian-style main house used for professional gatherings and boasts Skywalker Sound, operating since 1987. With amenities like themed guest rooms, diverse dining options, and a health club, the ranch remains a unique filmmaking destination, nearly fifty years after its inception.

Malkin reflected on their shared history, rivalry and friendship while acknowledging the significance of Ovechkin’s decision. The moment added another emotional layer to one of the NHL’s defining rivalries.

description: Carlos Alcaraz marked his remarkable comeback by successfully defending his Japan Open title against Jiri Lehecka, winning 7-6(4), 6-4. Delighted to hoist the trophy again, Alcaraz shared insights into the mental resilience required during his five-month recovery from injury. With renewed vigour, he eagerly anticipates competing in the Shanghai Masters next.

title: HC sends notice to Salman for his response on plea seeking stay on 'Kala Hiran'
description: The Delhi High Court is currently seeking input from Salman Khan regarding the lawsuit tied to 'Kala Hiran: The Battle for Legal'. The film's producers contend that his legal proceedings infringe upon an earlier claim about his personality rights. An injunction favoring Salman was granted in December 2025, resulting in protracted legal disputes.

title: US, China in talks for reciprocal visits to nuclear sites in bid to build trust
description: The United States intends to begin reciprocal visits to nuclear facilities in China, aiming to strengthen trust between the two nations. This proactive initiative seeks to avert a possible arms race amidst escalating worries over China's expanding nuclear arsenal. Currently, officials from both sides are engaging in preliminary talks. A pivotal meeting between US and Chinese leaders is expected later this year to enhance dialogue surrounding nuclear risks and capabilities.

title: Live-in relationships in India: What legal rights do partners have? FAQs explained
description: In India, live-in relationships hold a legal status that provides certain rights to each partner, though they are not classified as marriage. The judiciary evaluates these relationships by considering aspects like duration and shared duties. Women can pursue maintenance or domestic violence protection if necessary. Children from such unions have rights to inherit their parents' property under specific conditions, emphasizing the need for clear legal documentation to navigate these complexities.

title: From SME fund to hailing PM’s 25 years as govt head: Cabinet decisions & resolutions
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi led the Union Cabinet in approving innovative strategies to bolster small businesses and enhance transport infrastructure. The introduction of a Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund aims to empower small and medium enterprises in their growth and tech advancements. Moreover, the formation of the Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority seeks to streamline India's logistics and transport operations.

title: India, Qatar among seven bidders as race to host 2036 Olympics takes shape
description: India has been confirmed as a bidder for the 2036 Olympics along with six other nations. The International Olympic Committee is set to select the host in a vote scheduled for 2029. India's proposal centers around Ahmedabad, which aims to leverage its experience hosting events like the Commonwealth Games. Other bidders include Qatar, South Korea, and Germany among others striving for the prestigious event.

title: DNA from Siberian bones reveals previously unknown extinct relative of modern yaks
Boost for aerial surveillance: DRDO conducts flight-trial of high-altitude platform
description: The Defence Research and Development Organisation successfully conducted a flight trial of a high-altitude platform, reaching an impressive altitude of 21 kilometers and sustaining flight at 20 kilometers for over thirty minutes. This platform is aimed at enhancing long-endurance aerial surveillance and intelligence gathering. Flight data analysis revealed that it met performance expectations. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh hailed this development as a significant step toward India's self-reliance.

title: World's most-valuable company Nvidia now runs 'much more like a family business'
description: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's son-in-law Nico Caprez, a former Swiss ski racer, has become one of the chipmaker's most trusted executives, The Information reports. Caprez, who married Madison Huang in Hawaii last month, handles Nvidia's multibillion-dollar neocloud deals. Madison leads physical AI marketing, while son Spencer works in robotics. Some employees say the world's most valuable company now runs much more like a family business.

title: Your feed isn't random. The algorithm is built to keep you angry, anxious & scrolling
description: The newspaper gave you the world's bad news and then let you go. Your phone gives you the same news and keeps you there. Here is how that happened, what it is doing to us, and why countries are beginning to step in.

title: France student protests trigger school blockades, clashes and arrests -video
'Attacks must end': MEA says 11 Indian crew members injured in Hormuz vessel strike
Rare Nintendo cartridge found at New York garage sale later sold for $20,100
description: In an astounding find, video game enthusiast Rob Walters stumbled upon a rare Nintendo Campus Challenge cartridge at a garage sale back in 2006. This unique cartridge was made for a competitive gaming event in 1991 and hosted modified versions of beloved titles, allowing players to achieve high scores during tournaments.

title: From US' HACM to India's BrahMos-II: The world's hypersonic arms race heats up
description: The US Air Force's Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile has commenced its flight-test phase in Australia. This program has faced delays, prompting a reduction in overall testing plans to adhere to schedules. Developed alongside the Royal Australian Air Force, it aims for rapid acquisition decisions by 2027. India's hypersonic ambitions are also advancing, recently highlighted by successful testing of a scramjet vehicle.

title: Germany arrests former spy chief over treason and espionage allegations
Gene Hackman’s former LA estate sold for $1.71m; now asks $5.995m
description: A nearly 100-year-old English-style manor in Woodland Hills is listed for sale at $5.995 million. Originally built in 1928, the property has hosted notable owners like Michael Curtiz and Gene Hackman. The manor features a cobblestone driveway, extensive gardens, and original architectural details that reflect its rich history. Since its last sale in 1994 for $1.71 million, the property's value has significantly increased.

title: Abhishek, Shafali among 4 Indians nominated for ICC Player of the Month awards
description: September saw a stellar performance from Shubman Gill and Abhishek Sharma, both nominated for the ICC Player of the Month. Gill shone with 333 runs in ODIs, featuring a remarkable double-century against the West Indies. Abhishek dazzled in T20Is with 229 runs and set a record for the fastest century. Additionally, Shafali Verma and Shree Charani received praise for their outstanding contributions during a thrilling competition.

title: Andy Roddick and Brooklyn Decker bought Austin estate for $3.7m, sold for $4.65m
description: After extensive renovations, Andy Roddick and Brooklyn Decker sold their sprawling 15-acre estate in Austin, Texas. They bought the property in 2013 for about $3.7 million, and in 2019 sold it for approximately $4.65 million. The property showcased their tastes and aimed to be a family-friendly haven. The couple continues to hold several properties nationwide, including in North Carolina, while still thinking of Austin as home.

title: Vashishtha Narayan Singh: From Bihar village to Berkeley and global fame
description: Vashishtha Narayan Singh rose from a poor family in Bihar’s Bhojpur district to become a celebrated mathematician who earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. His exceptional talent took him from Netarhat and Patna to academic positions in the US and India. However, his later life was marked by schizophrenia, personal hardship and years of declining health. Singh died in 2019, leaving behind a complex legacy of remarkable intellectual achievement and adversity.

title: Jeffrey Archer: The Brit author who made Indians fall in love with English writing
description: Archer spent half a century writing about conmen, politicians, tycoons, rogues and impossible comebacks. In the end, none of his protagonists was quite as improbable, indefatigable or entertaining as Jeffrey Archer himself.

title: Crystal Cove estate bought for $30m sells 7 months later for $38.9m
Amid SIR protests, Delhi Police issue body-worn cameras to frontline personnel
description: Delhi Police has issued body-worn cameras to officers deployed in New Delhi for crowd control at protests. This decision comes amid complaints of police misconduct during recent protests against the Election Commission of India. A Public Interest Litigation has been filed to mandate the use of bodycams for police personnel involved in managing protests.

title: 103-year-old WWII veteran still tends same Maryland bar after 63 years
description: Irv Koch, a 103-year-old World War II veteran, has tended the bar in the basement of his Pasadena, Maryland, home since 1963. More than six decades later, the cash-only tavern still has no fixed opening hours, with Irv starting the day when his first customer arrives and closing when patrons leave or he gets tired.

title: From climbing barricades to Akashvani Bhawan twist: How Rahul-led CEC protest unfolded
Nobel Prize in Physics 2026: Francis Halzen awarded for work on cosmic neutrinos
description: Francis Halzen has received the Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 for his groundbreaking research at the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. This pivotal work has led to the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from cosmic sources, enhancing our comprehension of the universe. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences recognizes his efforts with an award of 12 million Swedish kronor.

title: Bus conductor took his suitcase, it vanished: 11 years later, commission orders Rs 43k
description: The Uttarakhand state consumer commission found the bus conductor negligent for losing a passenger's suitcase. The passenger filed a complaint after his suitcase went missing on a Delhi-Dehradun bus journey in 2015. Initially awarded Rs 57,500, the compensation was reduced to Rs 25,000 when the passenger failed to prove actual costs. The transport corporation must pay Rs 43,000 in total compensation and litigation charges.

title: Delaware homeowner wins court order in dispute over HOA records, maintenance
description: In a noteworthy court case, Gwendolyn Colston took on her community developer without legal representation and secured a favorable ruling. The Delaware Court of Chancery instructed the developer to ensure the upkeep of ponds and drainage systems in the area. Additionally, Colston gained access to insights on a contentious $44,329.

title: In 1934, America created a $1 duck stamp; it has protected 6 million acres
Florida mom rides 7,000 miles across 48 states, donates $17,560 to family support home
description: A Florida woman completed a 7,000-mile motorcycle journey across 48 states in six days. She raised $17,560 for Quantum House, an organization that supported her during her daughter’s hospital stay. The ride attracted attention, allowing her to create awareness about the organization. Jess's daughter, who benefitted from Quantum House, joined her when she presented the raised funds.

title: 'Wanted to tarnish image': Police on man held over AI poster showing cop assaulting woman
description: Delhi Police arrested a 24-year-old man named Nadeem Ahmed for creating a fake poster featuring a police officer. Police said the poster falsely depicted the officer sexually assaulting a woman during a protest, intending to damage police credibility. Investigators said Nadeem claimed to be an independent journalist and used AI tools for his misleading content.

title: Airbnb was born with 3 airbeds; 20 years later, it’s building 201 homes
description: Airbnb announced a $6.4 million investment for 201 affordable housing units in Austin, Texas. This initiative aims to address housing shortages and support the local community. The funding will assist in the construction of a broader development comprising mixed-income homes and retail spaces. Additionally, Airbnb is collaborating with local organizations to advocate for pro-housing policies. The involvement of Airbnb seeks to create sustainable and affordable housing solutions in the city.

title: Watch: Rahul climbs barricades, waves Tricolour as cops stop INDIA bloc march against CEC
Travis & Jason Kelce donate $10K to $50K Olympic fundraiser family reunion
description: Earlier this year, Travis and Jason Kelce quietly donated $10,000 to help a Team USA hockey star’s family travel to Milan for the 2026 Winter Olympics. The contribution supported a $50,000 fundraiser created after the family struggled to afford the trip. Travis also offered encouragement before the Olympic debut, while Jason and Kylie attended the gold-medal game. Team USA eventually defeated Canada 2-1 in overtime for gold.

title: Naomi Osaka’s family mission to help children in Haiti began in 1999
description: Naomi Osaka's heartfelt bond with Haiti is rooted in her family's foundation, which was formed in 1999 to uplift the community. Her inaugural trip to Haiti occurred in October 2017, followed by another visit after her first Grand Slam win in 2018. Engaging with local children, she championed educational initiatives and allocated part of her earnings for earthquake relief. This connection deeply influences Osaka's ongoing philanthropic endeavors.
